title: How to move cursor without mouse in Cursor on Mac for efficient keyboard navigation
metaTitle: Move Cursor Without Mouse in Cursor on Mac: Guide
description: Learn how to move the cursor on Mac without a mouse while using the Cursor IDE. Follow our step-by-step guide to enable macOS Mouse Keys for your workflow.
targetKeyword: move cursor on mac without mouse
intro: To move the cursor on Mac without a mouse while using Cursor, you must enable the macOS Mouse Keys accessibility feature. This system-level setting allows you to control the pointer using your keyboard keys instead of a physical mouse or trackpad.
tldr: Open System Settings on your Mac.
Navigate to Accessibility and select Pointer Control.
Use your keyboard to move the pointer and click.
Press the Option key five times to toggle this mode quickly.

blocks.text: Why use keyboard navigation in Cursor

Many developers prefer to keep their hands on the keyboard to maintain flow. When you move the cursor on Mac without a mouse, you reduce the time lost reaching for your trackpad. This is especially useful in Cursor, where you frequently switch between editing code and interacting with AI agents.

Cursor is built on the VS Code architecture. It does not have a native mouse-replacement tool. Relying on macOS system features is the most reliable way to gain this control. Once you master the key mappings, you will find it easier to perform precise UI interactions.
How to enable Mouse Keys on macOS
Mouse Keys is a universal feature. It works in every application, including Cursor. Follow these steps to activate it on your Mac.

items: Open the Apple Menu () and select System Settings.
Click on Accessibility in the sidebar.
Find the Motor section and click Pointer Control.
Locate Mouse Keys and toggle the switch to On.
Click the info (i) button to customize your activation shortcut.

blocks.text: Using keyboard keys as a mouse

Once enabled, specific keys on your keyboard become mouse controls. Note that these keys will stop typing their normal characters while Mouse Keys is active. You must toggle the mode off when you need to type code.

You might find that your custom Cursor shortcuts conflict with system accessibility settings. Use the Option key five times to toggle Mouse Keys on and off instantly. This is the fastest way to switch between mouse-free navigation and typing mode.

If you notice that Option + Left or Right Arrow keys stop working for word-by-word movement in the terminal, check your settings. Ensure terminal.integrated.macOptionIsMeta is configured correctly in your Cursor settings menu.

If you are working on a laptop without a dedicated numeric keypad, use the letter keys (U, I, O, J, K, L) as mapped in the table above. This allows for comfortable navigation without external hardware.

faq.question: Does Cursor have a built-in mouse replacement?
faq.answer: No. Cursor does not include a built-in tool to move the mouse cursor. You must use the macOS Mouse Keys feature to achieve this.

faq.question: Will Mouse Keys stop me from typing?
faq.answer: Yes. When Mouse Keys is active, the keys assigned to movement will not type characters. Use the Option key shortcut (pressing it five times) to toggle the feature off quickly when you need to write code.

faq.question: Can I use this in the Cursor web interface?
faq.answer: Mouse Keys is a system-level feature, but browser-based apps have different focus behaviors. For the best experience, use the desktop version of Cursor.

task: Enable Mouse Keys on macOS to navigate Cursor without a mouse.

steps.name: Open System Settings
steps.text: Click the Apple icon in the top left corner of your screen and select System Settings.

steps.name: Access Accessibility
steps.text: Find and click on the Accessibility tab in the left sidebar.

steps.name: Configure Pointer Control
steps.text: Select Pointer Control from the list of options to see mouse settings.

steps.name: Enable Mouse Keys
steps.text: Toggle the Mouse Keys switch to the On position.
steps.tip: Click the info icon next to the switch to set up the five-press Option key shortcut.

troubleshooting.problem: Keys are not moving the mouse cursor.
troubleshooting.fix: Check System Settings to ensure Mouse Keys is actually toggled on. If you are on a laptop, ensure you are using the letter keys (U, I, O, K) instead of the numeric keypad keys.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot type letters in my code editor.
troubleshooting.fix: This is normal while Mouse Keys is active. Press the Option key five times to turn the feature off so you can type again.
